Arms, all over a REAL store via ../bootstrap/bootstrap-test-fixtures.js:
 1. `answers nulls, with the exact key roster, while nothing is bound` — driveThrough(store,"repository.publish") (i.e. STOPS BEFORE it) then toEqual({boundAt:null,boundBy:null,outcome:"REMOTE",readAt:NOW,remoteUrl:null}) AND `Object.keys(...).sort()` toEqual ["boundAt","boundBy","outcome","readAt","remoteUrl"] — the roster restated by hand at the point of use (VIEW_KEYS :38), not derived from the value it checks.
 2. `carries the binding the real publish committed, verbatim` — driveThrough(store,"goal.close") runs the PRODUCTION `repository.publish` handler (no hand-appended event), then the view carries {boundAt:"2026-08-08T00:00:00.000Z", boundBy:"principal-1", remoteUrl:"https://github.com/fixture/repo.git"} verbatim; plus `boundBy` is asserted NOT to equal GOOD_CREDENTIAL (it is a principal id, never a credential).
 3. `keeps two projects on one store from seeing each other's remote` — a port on the same store bound to "project-2" reads all-nulls (the aggregate id carries the projectId).
 4. `refuses UNREADABLE, with its own layer, when the fold throws` — injected readRemote that throws => {code:"REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_UNREADABLE", layer:"REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ", outcome:"REFUSED"} — CODE AND LAYER, per global rail 1 — and the CODES roster asserted in order.
 5. handler arms (one it, five expects): PLANNING credential => body REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED + layer + httpStatus 200; port absent => {code:"LISTENER_REPOSITORY_REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE", kind:"LISTENER_REFUSAL"}; boundProjectId "elsewhere" => REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PROJECT_MISMATCH; body `{"x":1}` => LISTENER_REPOSITORY_REMOTE_REQUEST_INVALID; empty Uint8Array AND `{} \n` (trailing whitespace) both forward to the port.
 6-8. the three `through the real listener` arms — those belong to step 5 and are recorded there.

Unbound vs unreadable are deliberately DIFFERENT answers: nothing bound is a legitimate `outcome:"REMOTE"` with nulls (the Publish control renders "no remote yet"); only a store that cannot be read refuses. Per child 1's handoff, a url that today's admission rule no longer admits reads as UNBOUND (nulls) rather than as a bad url, because readProjectRemote fails closed — so the view can never surface a url the daemon would refuse to push to.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Skill loaded and the full checklist walked against my own diff. ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED; the rest verified already-covered.

THE DEFECT — my module comment stated a contract the shipped code does not honour. It read: "Unbound and unreadable are DIFFERENT answers on purpose ... a store that cannot be read is a refusal." MEASURED FALSE. `readProjectRemote` (publish-ledger.ts:136-140) wraps `store.readEvents` in its own try/catch and RETURNS NULL on failure; `decodeBinding` likewise returns null for an undecodable payload or a url `admitRemoteUrl` no longer admits. So with the SHIPPED reader, a broken store, a corrupt binding and a retired url ALL render as the unbound view (all nulls under `outcome: "REMOTE"`), and REFUSED is reachable only when an INJECTED reader throws — never from a store fault. This matters beyond wording: child 3 (task-e6000b57) builds its decoder against this contract and would have waited for a refusal it can never receive.
  Verified by construction, not by reading: a `Proxy` over a REAL store whose `readEvents` throws (methods `.bind(target)` and `Reflect.get(target, prop, target)` so the store's `#private` state still resolves — child 1's technique). Result: the UNBOUND view, confirming the analysis.
  FIXED TWO WAYS, so the correction cannot rot: (a) the module comment now states what actually collapses into unbound and why it is deliberate fail-closed behaviour (surfacing a superseded remote would point a push at a repository the operator has already left); (b) a PERMANENT ARM, not a deleted probe (global rail 12): `reads an unreadable STORE as unbound, not as a refusal`, carrying a POSITIVE CONTROL — `expect(readProjectRemote(real, PROJECT_ID)).not.toBeNull()` — so the all-nulls answer is proven to be the injected fault and not an empty fixture. The pre-existing `refuses UNREADABLE ... when the fold throws` arm stays, pinning the other path. Both directions are now asserted.

THE REST OF THE CHECKLIST — each item verified against an EXISTING arm, none taken on faith:
- A bound url that today's rule no longer admits reads as null (child 1's rule): covered by the fix above; the view then says unbound, never a bad url.
- Constant cost: `readProjectRemote` calls `store.readEvents(remoteAggregateId(projectId))` — ONE aggregate, `remote:<projectId>`, no decision-page walk. Cost grows only with the number of REBINDS of one project's remote, not with decisions or goals.
- `boundBy` is a principal, never a credential: arm `carries the binding the real publish committed, verbatim` asserts the value is "principal-1" AND separately `.not.toBe(GOOD_CREDENTIAL)`.
- `{}` with trailing whitespace: arm asserts `{} \n` forwards (decodeBoundedJsonBytes accepts it, same as sessions); empty Uint8Array forwards too.
- Two projects on one store: arm `keeps two projects on one store from seeing each other's remote` — a port on the SAME store bound to "project-2" reads all-nulls, because the aggregate id carries the projectId.
- CONCURRENCY: nothing to race. The read is pure projection — no writes, no check-then-act, no shared mutable state; each `provider.repositoryRemote()` call constructs a fresh port and every result is `Object.freeze`d. Two concurrent reads cannot interfere.
- INPUTS: non-object, array, `null`, oversized and malformed bodies are all rejected by `emptyBody` (decodeBoundedJsonBytes is the bounded decoder, so a 1GB body is refused by the transport, not by this module) => LISTENER_REPOSITORY_REMOTE_REQUEST_INVALID; injection-shaped strings never reach a query — the aggregate id is composed from the daemon's OWN config projectId, never from the request body, which must be exactly `{}`.
- AUTH ASSUMPTIONS: not trusted-upstream. The handler authenticates FIRST, then requires CAPABILITIES.GOAL, then compares `access.principal.projectId` to the port's `boundProjectId`. Drill 2 proved the capability gate is pinned by CODE, not merely by "refused".
- SIDE EFFECTS / EXIT PATHS: no handles, sockets or subprocesses opened; the only failure path returns a frozen refusal. Idempotent — no retry hazard.
- EMBARRASSMENT TEST: the thing I would have been dinged for cold is exactly the comment defect above, and the drill-4 hole (a wiring key with no coverage), both now closed.

DAEMON SIDE LANDED (task-19d2329c, REVIEW). The symbols your read route consumes exist on the branch now — measured, not promised:

- `apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-ledger.ts`: `export function readProjectRemote(store: SqliteEventStore, projectId: string): ProjectRemote | null`, where `ProjectRemote = Readonly<{ remoteUrl: string; boundAt: string; boundBy: string }>` (also exported). Returns a FROZEN object or null. Null means "nothing usable is bound" and covers all four cases: no aggregate, no `RepositoryRemoteBound` event, an undecodable/extra-key payload, and a stored url that NO LONGER ADMITS. It deliberately does NOT fall back to an older binding when the LATEST one is unreadable — pushing to a superseded remote is the defect the read exists to prevent. A throwing store also yields null, no throw.
- `apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts`: `remoteAggregateId(projectId) => "remote:" + projectId`, `REMOTE_BOUND_EVENT_TYPE = "RepositoryRemoteBound"`.

FOR YOUR ROUTE SHAPE `{ outcome: "REMOTE", remoteUrl, boundAt, boundBy }`: the three nullable fields map 1:1 onto `readProjectRemote(...)` — when it answers null, all three are null TOGETHER. There is no partial state to encode: a binding with one bad field decodes as null in full, so a route that emitted e.g. a remoteUrl with a null boundAt would be describing a state the ledger cannot produce.
